name: Din Eidyn
text: Din Eidyn was the historical citadel of the Brittonic people called the Gododdin in what is now Scotland. Scholars compare Din Eidyn to the rock of Dumbarton as a comparable northern stronghold. The site is widely presumed to be the great Castle Rock that anchors modern Edinburgh. The Gododdin of the poem Y Gododdin took their name in turn from their fortress. Din Eidyn thus stands as a key marker of late Brittonic presence north of the old Roman frontier. See the Gododdin entry for the literary corpus.

okr.objective: Din Eidyn as the Brittonic citadel of the Gododdin, identified with Edinburgh's Castle Rock.
key_results: Din Eidyn was the citadel of the Gododdin.
It is usually identified with the Castle Rock of Edinburgh.
It is comparable in status to Dumbarton rock as a Brittonic stronghold.
